text.p: The pound held a one-pfennig and half-cent gain in late business after Treasury "wise-man" Tim Congdon called for a one point rise in British base interest rates.
The already firm pound touched $1.5930, its highest level since early October last year while sterling/mark hit 2.4568, its highest level since late December 1994.
In the UK's Evening Standard newspaper Congdon said a rise of "about one percent would be the right thing to do."
"If rates are raised soon, that will avert the need for more drastic moves at a later date," he said.
The next monetary meeting between Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England governor Eddie George is on October 30.
Dealers said it is hard to find people in the market who expect a rate rise ahead of next year's general election, let alone find someone who expects rates to rise a full percentage point.

Base lending rates are currently 5.75 percent and were last cut, by 25 basis points, on June 6. Dealers said cable was also pushed higher amid talk that a large option with a knock-out strike at $1.59 expired today.
The holder of the option had actively tried to hold sterling below that level until the option expired, dealers said.
"That added to the sterling move higher," said Alan Collins, head of technical analysis at Merita Bank.
Stering's trade weighted rose 0.3 point at 89.3.
